messages.body_plain:

Whenever there is Map Reduce kind of work going on (e.g., using datadr::drRead.csv() or datadr::divide()) on HDFS connection data, there is a message that says

‘Waiting 5 minutes’

I think the actual Map or Reduce task is gets interrupted (goes into sleep) for a while.

Is there a reason for this? I think this is happening at RHIPE level.

The system I am using is Amazon Web Service (AWS) Elastic Map Reduce (EMR) with v2.4.2 image.
RHIPE version is 0.74

Thanks in advance.

messages.subject: Re: ‘Waiting 5 minutes’
messages.body_plain:
I am using older AMI version because according to the EMR install page for Tessera <https://github.com/tesseradata/install-emr>  RHIPE v0.74 only works with Google Protobufs v2.4.1, and RHIPE v0.75 failed to work with Protobufs v2.5. According to the AMI versions in EMR <http://docs.aws.amazon.com/ElasticMapReduce/latest/DeveloperGuide/ami-versions-supported.html>,  AMI v3.0.3 is where Protobufs 2.5 got installed by default, so I use an older AMI.

I didn't modify the EMR scripts for installation of RHIPE and Protobufs. RHIPE is being downloaded from:
http://people.mozilla.com/~sguha/Rhipe_0.74.0_hadoop-1.tar.gz

Should I be grabbing the latest RHIPE directly from GitHub instead? In the setting up Tessera on a cluster <http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/docs/InstallCluster.pdf> PDF, RHIPE v0.74 is downloaded from Purdue University and it is also using Protobufs v2.4.1.

What version of AMI did you manage to deploy Tessera successfully with?

> We saw a problem similar to this about 9 months ago where the console would stop updating but the MR jobs would complete in the background. It happened only intermittently to us and only on Amazon EMR clusters, but we never figured out the cause. However it hasn't happened recently. Is there a particular reason you're using such old versions of AMI and Rhipe? It might help to update to the newest versions.

messages.body_plain:
This could be because RHIPE process doesn't have privileges to write to /tmp directory in Hadoop File System (HDFS).

Try to change the permission of /tmp directory in HDFS to allow read and write by all users and see if it works:

hadoop fs chmod 777 -R /tmp

messages.subject: Update
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

It's been a while since I've posted to the group.  I'm going to try to make it more of a practice to hop on the mailing list periodically to provide news of new developments in Tessera.

There's been a ton of activity going on, so much so that haven't left myself time for communication.  I put up a new post on the blog today covering some of the activity that has been going on recently: http://tessera.io/blog/tessera-update/.  I hope to be doing a lot more posting in the near future.

Also, I've been having a great deal of personal correspondences regarding Tessera.  I'm going to start trying to direct those to the mailing list so that they are useful for others.

This mailing list is a great place to ask questions or show off things you have been working on.  Please don't be afraid to jump in!

Ryan

messages.subject: trelliscope crashing in Windows
messages.body_plain:
I have made some trelliscope displays in one vdb connection.  I copied the vdb folder to a share drive and my coworker is able to view the trelliscope displays using R (so no web syncing).  However, her R session repeatedly crashes and does so more quickly each time.  Meaning the first time she could view the displays for minutes to hours before R crashed.  Now it crashes nearly upon viewing the displays.  The only hint at the real problem that I have is that it may have something to do with Rsync.  Below are specifics regarding her machine and R session.  The crash occurs in Rstudio or regular R.
Let me know what else I can provide that might help clarify the problem and a possible solution.  Thank you for your efforts.  I use dataDR and Trelliscope daily now and my coworker will soon be doing the same.
Trenton
801-230-7499

# R code

library(trelliscope)

library(datadr)

library(ggplot2)

library(reshape2)

library(GGally)

library(matlab)

conn=vdbConn("N:/Trenton/MissionaryOptimizeComplements/vdb1", name = "vdb1")

view()
